question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x+4} & ={6}^{2-3x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x+4}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{2-3x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}\end{aligned}
$$
